results.name: agentic-rag
results.title: Agentic RAG
results.summary: Agentic RAG wraps a vector-database retriever as a tool for an LLM agent, which reformulates queries, critiques retrieved snippets, and iterates through multiple retrieval rounds before synthesizing an answer

results.name: rag-architecture-decision-tree
results.title: RAG Architecture Decision Tree
results.summary: Diagnostic framework for choosing among 8 RAG architectures (Naive, Hybrid, Reranked, Multi-Query, Hierarchical, Corrective, Graph, Agentic) based on observed failure modes — treat RAG like debugging: let Naive fail first, watch how it fails, then pick the architecture that fixes that specific symptom; measure retrieval separately from generation

results.name: contextual-retrieval-anthropic
results.title: Contextual Retrieval (Anthropic Cookbook)
results.summary: Demonstrates three progressive techniques for improving RAG retrieval quality — contextual embeddings (situating each chunk within its source document before embedding), contextual BM25 hybrid search, and reranking — achieving up to 95.26% Pass@10

results.name: rag-retrieval-recipe
results.title: RAG Retrieval Recipe
results.summary: Practitioner's RAG recipe — semantic chunking (500-1000 tokens, 100 overlap), embed once with nomic/mxbai, store in ChromaDB/Qdrant/LanceDB, retrieve top-20 → BGE rerank → top-5, cite source chunks in LLM output

results.name: agentic-rag-terminal-tools
results.title: Agentic RAG with Terminal Tools (Direct Corpus Interaction)
results.summary: Research pattern where LLM agents with terminal tool access (grep, find, head, cat) outperform embedding-based retrieval across 13+ benchmarks — Direct Corpus Interaction (DCI) removes embedding model, vector index, and top-k retrieval entirely; adopted by Anthropic (Claude Code), Windsurf, Cline, Devin, Sourcegraph Amp

results.name: production-rag-system-taxonomy
results.title: Production RAG as a System (8-Part Taxonomy)
results.summary: Practitioner taxonomy framing production RAG as an 8-part system (not a vector-database feature): 01 offline build time (parse/chunk/embed/index), 02 online query time (rewrite/retrieve/rerank/assemble/generate), 03 knowledge store (vectors+metadata+raw docs+freshness), 04 retrieval quality (hybrid search/filters/top-k/reranking), 05 answer quality (grounding/citations/structured output/fallback), 06 state/data layer (Postgres+Redis+object storage+vector index), 07 observability/evals (latency/recall/answer quality/hallucinations/cost), 08 safety operations (ACLs/PII protection/prompt-injection defense/caching/feedback); presented as a directory-tree mental model contrasting with the four-step chunk-embed-retrieve-prompt demo pipeline.

results.name: pageindex
results.title: PageIndex
results.summary: Vectorless reasoning-based RAG engine — replaces vector index with hierarchical tree index, uses LLM reasoning for retrieval instead of similarity search; 98.7% accuracy on FinanceBench (vs vector RAG baselines); SDK with local mode (pip install pageindex) and cloud mode; ~$0.001/page indexing cost; ideal for financial/legal/medical/technical documents; MIT

results.name: ovis-vl-embedding
results.title: Ovis-VL-Embedding
results.summary: Omni-modal embedding model (2B and 9B variants) built on Qwen3.5 backbone — encodes text, images, visual documents, and video frames in a shared representation space; 77.46 overall on MMEB-v2 (78 datasets), 80.47 on visual document retrieval; no modality-specific projection heads, last-token hidden state as embedding; for multimodal RAG, cross-modal search, document retrieval

results.name: dify
results.title: Dify
results.summary: Dify provides a visual drag-and-drop interface for building AI applications, combining workflow orchestration, RAG document ingestion/retrieval, agent tool use with 50+ built-in tools, model management, and production observability (LLMOps) into a single self-hostable platform

results.name: sira-superintelligent-retrieval-agent
results.title: SIRA — Superintelligent Retrieval Agent
results.summary: Meta research framework that compresses multi-round agentic retrieval into a single corpus-discriminative BM25 action — LLM enriches documents offline with missing vocabulary, predicts query-side evidence terms, validates via IDF tool calls, then issues one weighted sparse retrieval; outperforms dense retrievers and multi-round agents on BEIR/NQ/HotpotQA with no fine-tuning

results.name: rag-anything
results.title: RAG-Anything
results.summary: All-in-one multimodal RAG framework from HKU's Data Intelligence Lab, built on LightRAG — parses PDFs/Office/images/audio/video via MinerU, Docling, or PaddleOCR, then builds a multimodal knowledge graph linking text, tables, equations, and images; three query modes (text, VLM-enhanced, direct multimodal); 23,500+ GitHub stars; MIT

results.name: vector-distance-metrics-cheatsheet
results.title: Vector Embeddings Distance Metrics Cheat Sheet
results.summary: Practitioner cheat sheet on choosing vector distance metrics for RAG: cosine similarity (unnormalized text), dot product (fastest for normalized unit vectors), L2 Euclidean (clustering); plus Matryoshka trick — truncate embedding dimensions from 1536→512 to cut vector RAM by 80% with minimal accuracy loss

results.name: tolvi
results.title: Tolvi — Engineering Decision Vault
results.summary: Solid CAG/RAG dual-mode decision-capture design but pre-1.0, small project, and overlaps with kb already in use

results.name: onyx-ai-platform
results.title: Onyx AI Platform
results.summary: Full self-hostable AI platform with agentic RAG and MCP — notable architecture reference, but too deployment-heavy to adopt as a composable toolkit component

results.name: chunkless-rag
results.title: Chunkless RAG (IBM)
results.summary: RAG architecture that preserves document tree structure instead of splitting into fixed-size chunks — AI agents navigate the document hierarchy (table of contents, headings, sections) like a human reader, reading short section summaries to locate relevant content, then drilling into specific sections; requires structural document parsing (e.g. Docling) to reconstruct logical hierarchy from PDFs; trades higher latency and compute for better cross-section reasoning, context preservation, and reduced hallucination on complex documents

results.name: sira
results.title: SIRA (Superintelligent Retrieval Agent)
results.summary: Meta (FAIR) research pipeline that uses LLMs to enrich both documents and queries to improve BM25 retrieval without training. Five stages: data prep, BM25 indexing, corpus enrichment (LLM indexing phrases), query expansion (LLM search terms), and LLM pointwise reranking; reports SOTA on BEIR using only inference-time compute. MIT.

results.name: graphrag-agent-memory-linkedin-series
results.title: GraphRAG & Agent Memory LinkedIn Series
results.summary: Six-post series covering GraphRAG design, ontology modeling, and unified agent memory architecture — useful conceptual grounding for KG-backed agents.

results.name: five-levels-of-chunking
results.title: Five Levels of Chunking Strategies in RAG (Greg Kamradt's taxonomy)
results.summary: Taxonomy of RAG text-splitting strategies, from Greg Kamradt's '5 Levels of Text Splitting' (these are notes on that video): Level 1 fixed-size (character/sentence splitters), Level 2 recursive (hierarchical separators), Level 3 document/structure-based (respect headings, tables, code), Level 4 semantic (split at embedding-similarity breakpoints), Level 5 agentic (an LLM decides chunk boundaries from propositions). Higher levels trade cost/complexity for chunks that better match meaning; match the strategy to the data.

results.name: llama-index
results.title: LlamaIndex
results.summary: Open-source Python data framework for building LLM/RAG and document-agent apps: data connectors, indices/graphs, retrievers, and query engines to augment LLMs with private data, with 300+ integration packages (LLMs, embeddings, vector stores) on LlamaHub. Pairs with the commercial LlamaParse/Parse agentic-OCR platform. MIT.

results.name: three-store-hybrid-memory-architecture
results.title: 3-Store Hybrid Memory Architecture for AI Agents
results.summary: An architecture pattern arguing vector embeddings alone fail for AI agent memory, proposing three parallel stores — a vector store for fuzzy semantic matching, a key-value store for exact fact lookup, and a knowledge graph for multi-hop relationship reasoning — merged by a fusion layer

results.name: chromadb
results.title: ChromaDB
results.summary: Open-source AI search infrastructure with vector, full-text, regex, and hybrid search — embedding-agnostic with Python/JS SDKs, serverless cloud option, and multi-modal retrieval; strong fit for literature/sequence RAG pipelines

results.name: claude-cookbook
results.title: Claude Cookbook
results.summary: Anthropic's official collection of 60+ practical guides covering agent patterns, tool use, RAG, managed agents, Agent SDK, evals, and multimodal — the authoritative how-to reference for Claude API development

results.name: cross-encoder-reranking
results.title: Cross-Encoder Reranking for RAG
results.summary: Second-stage retrieval technique: a cross-encoder jointly encodes a query and one candidate document in a single transformer forward pass, using self-attention across both texts to produce one relevance score per pair — more accurate but far more expensive than first-stage bi-encoder vector search, so it only reorders a small top-k candidate set rather than scoring a whole corpus.

results.name: prompt-assembly-cache-discipline
results.title: Prompt Assembly and Cache Discipline
results.summary: Rules for LLM prompt assembly that preserve KV-cache efficiency — never rewrite the front of a prompt (invalidates cached tokens), avoid sliding windows that evict oldest turns (same cost), cap fat messages in-place to stay cacheable, put retrieval/per-query content last as a suffix so changes do not poison the cached prefix; includes five-layer assembler concept and ablation methodology

results.name: six-ai-engineer-projects
results.title: Six AI Engineer Skills as Six Named Company Problems
results.summary: Curriculum-as-project-list framing six AI engineering skills as named, production-shaped builds: RAG (Fieldnote — answers from the chart on page 112, not its caption), Agents (Casefile — claims triage with typed handoffs, cost ceiling, human before payout), LLMOps (Warmstart — 3-layer cache over 400k questions/month with measured false-hit rate), Evals (Groundtruth — legal-research harness failing the PR when recall drops), Fine-tuning (Slotfill — LoRA on 40k freight invoices benchmarked against the prompt it replaces), Guardrails (Doorman — recruiting agent surviving resume-embedded injection)

results.name: ai-engineering-hub
results.title: AI Engineering Hub
results.summary: Curated collection of 93+ hands-on tutorial projects for LLM/RAG/agent engineering, organized by difficulty (beginner/intermediate/advanced), covering OCR, chat UIs, RAG variants, MCP integrations, model comparisons, fine-tuning, and production agent systems

results.name: isaacflath-ocr-guides
results.title: Isaac Flath — Documents in AI Products (OCR Pipeline Guides)
results.summary: 14-post blog series covering OCR model selection, VLM OCR, speculative decoding, PDF retrieval, chunking, quantization, and document QA — practical guidelines for designing OCR pipelines

results.name: fluxmem
results.title: FluxMem: Continuously Evolving Memory Connectivity
results.summary: FluxMem is a memory architecture for AI agents that treats memory as an evolving graph of interconnected semantic, episodic, and procedural nodes, with runtime self-repair (link expansion/pruning, content reshaping) and offline consolidation into reusable skills

results.name: redis-iris
results.title: Redis Iris
results.summary: Redis's context-and-memory platform for AI agents (announced May 18, 2026) — bundles real-time structured/unstructured data retrieval (Context Retriever), short- and long-term agent memory (Agent Memory: interaction history, user preferences, persistent attributes), and continuous data sync from source-of-record systems (Redis Data Integration) into one product, layered on existing Redis Search and LangCache semantic caching

results.name: claude-projects
results.title: Claude Projects
results.summary: Anthropic support documentation for Claude Projects — persistent workspaces with an uploaded-file knowledge base and custom instructions across claude.ai chat, Cowork, and Claude Code, plus a September 2026 beta redesign (Claude Code first) that turns a project into one coordinator conversation dispatching parallel cloud-hosted worker threads

results.name: docling-mcp
results.title: Docling MCP
results.summary: MCP server for document conversion, processing, and generation via the Docling library — converts PDFs and other documents into structured DoclingDocument JSON with OCR, table structure detection, and image handling; supports local, remote (Docling Serve), and hybrid modes; RAG integrations with Milvus, LlamaIndex, and LlamaStack; LF AI & Data project from IBM Research Zurich, MIT, 730+ stars

results.name: pixelrag
results.title: PixelRAG
results.summary: Open-source RAG framework from Berkeley Sky Computing Lab/BAIR/Berkeley NLP that renders web pages, PDFs, and images to screenshot tiles and retrieves over the images directly (via a LoRA-fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B model) instead of parsing text, preserving tables/charts/layout; supports text or image queries; ships a hosted API over a pre-built 8.28M-page Wikipedia index, a Claude Code plugin (pixelbrowse) that lets Claude screenshot and read a page instead of fetching raw HTML, FAISS or Qdrant backends, and a separate LoRA training pipeline; Apache-2.0

results.name: knowledge-folder-behavior-model-split
results.title: Knowledge in the Folder, Behavior in the Model: A Fine-Tuning vs. RAG Split
results.summary: A three-step strategy for deciding what to fine-tune versus what to retrieve: keep facts (pricing, policies, specs) in documents the model reads at answer time rather than baking them into weights, since fine-tuning changes model behavior, not factual recall, so tuning on company documents still produces factual errors; tune only for behavior (output format, tone, how to answer a complaint) using a few hundred clean, human-approved examples of one task rather than thousands of unreviewed ones; and do that tuning on a small open-weight model run on a single workstation, A/B tested against the untuned baseline before deployment.

results.name: ai-memory-comparison
results.title: AI Memory Comparison
results.summary: Definitive source-backed survey of 73 open-source AI agent memory systems across 79 features — every claim cites public code or docs.

results.name: amazon-bedrock
results.title: Amazon Bedrock
results.summary: AWS managed platform for building generative AI applications — 100+ foundation models (Amazon Nova, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT-5.x, Meta Llama, DeepSeek, Mistral, etc.) through one API; AgentCore for production agent deployment with any framework (LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, Strands); Knowledge Bases for RAG; Guardrails; model distillation, prompt caching, intelligent routing; enterprise security (SOC, ISO, FedRAMP High, HIPAA eligible)

results.name: pinecone
results.title: Pinecone
results.summary: Fully managed, closed-source serverless vector database — proprietary Rust engine separates compute from storage, consumption-based pricing (~$0.33/GB-month storage plus metered read/write units), targets ~200ms query latency at 80% p95 recall; offers hosted embedding/reranking (Pinecone Inference), Pinecone Assistant, Dedicated Read Nodes, and Bring-Your-Own-Cloud for data residency; no self-hosting option.

results.name: azure-ai-foundry-chat-starter
results.title: Get Started with AI Chat (Azure AI Foundry)
results.summary: Microsoft starter template that deploys a RAG-capable chat web app to Azure Container Apps using Microsoft Foundry models and Azure AI Search for file-grounded, cited responses; deployable via azd up or a guided Copilot CLI /up skill; explicitly marked not production-ready without added security hardening

results.name: chroma
results.title: Chroma
results.summary: AI-native open-source embedding database — 4-function core API, automatic tokenization/embedding/indexing, metadata filtering, in-memory or persistent modes, SIMD-accelerated maxscore, sharding, group-by aggregation, Python/JS/Go clients; Chroma Cloud for managed serverless; Apache-2.0

results.name: embeddinggemma-2
results.title: EmbeddingGemma 2
results.summary: Google DeepMind's 740M-parameter open multimodal embedding model — maps text, code, images, video, and audio into one 768-dim vector space; modular encoders (270M text-only to 740M full); 8K context window; runs on-device (191MB RAM for text-only on Pixel 11 Pro); Matryoshka truncation to 512/256/128 dims; built on Gemma 4; Apache 2.0

results.name: vector-database-cost-economics
results.title: Vector Database Cost Economics
results.summary: Practitioner cost model for vector databases: storage bytes = vector count × dimensions × precision (1M 768-dim float32 vectors ≈ 3GB before index/metadata overhead; dimensions scale storage linearly, so 3072-dim embeddings cost 4x what 768-dim cost); RAM-resident indexes cost roughly 10-50x more per GB than SSD, which is roughly 10x object storage (~$0.023/GB-month raw S3-class rate); production replication (2-3x) and HNSW-style index overhead (1.5-2x raw vector bytes) compound on top; query/write pricing (per-request, per-unit, or folded into storage) can dominate the bill at high QPS independent of storage cost.

results.name: microsoft-eval-guide
results.title: Microsoft Eval Guide
results.summary: A Claude Code plugin providing six skills that walk through a five-stage evaluation lifecycle (discover, plan, generate & baseline, run, interpret & improve) for AI agents built on Microsoft Copilot Studio, with architecture-aware scoping and interactive HTML dashboards

results.name: unstructured
results.title: Unstructured
results.summary: Open-source document ETL library — partitions 60+ file types (PDFs, Word, HTML, images, emails) into structured elements (Title, NarrativeText, Table, etc.) with layout ML enrichment, OCR, chunking, and embedding; connectors for 40+ sources/destinations; MCP server (Unstructured Transform) for agent-driven document processing; Apache-2.0, 15k+ stars

results.name: mmeb-benchmark
results.title: MMEB — Massive Multimodal Embedding Benchmark
results.summary: Comprehensive benchmark for evaluating omni-modality embedding models — V1 covers 36 image-text datasets across classification/VQA/retrieval/grounding; V2 adds video and visual document tasks (78 total); V3 extends to audio, text retrieval, and agent-centric tasks (190 total); introduced alongside VLM2Vec; TIGER-AI-Lab, ICLR 2025 → TMLR/COLM 2026

results.name: google-knowledge-catalog
results.title: Google Cloud Knowledge Catalog
results.summary: Google Cloud's Gemini-powered data catalog and metadata management platform (formerly Dataplex); builds a dynamic context graph of structured/unstructured data assets for AI agent grounding, with MCP server integration for context retrieval

results.name: tencentdb-agent-memory
results.title: TencentDB Agent Memory
results.summary: Tencent-built team-level memory hub for AI agents providing four asset types — layered Chat Memory (L0-L3), versioned Skills, linked Wiki pages, and a CodeGraph — managed through a human-reviewable Memory Hub panel with ACL-based sharing

results.name: weaviate
results.title: Weaviate
results.summary: Go-based AI-native vector database — stores objects with vectors, integrated vectorization via OpenAI/Cohere/HuggingFace modules, semantic + BM25 keyword + hybrid search, built-in RAG and reranking, ACORN filtered search, multi-tenancy with RBAC, object TTL, gRPC/REST/GraphQL APIs; BSD-3-Clause

results.name: mixpeek
results.title: Mixpeek
results.summary: Multimodal search/retrieval infrastructure ('multimodal data warehouse') running on object storage: typed feature-extraction pipelines turn video/files into queryable timestamped features (scenes, transcripts, faces, OCR, fingerprints), embeddings are generated/stored from 50+ models, and multi-stage retrievers compose filter/join/rerank (advertised <100ms). Integrations include S3, GCS, R2, Mux, LangChain, and MCP. Catalog source is a Mixpeek education video contrasting an 'extract once, upstream of every app' model against a plain vector database.

results.name: agent-dispatcher
results.title: Agent Dispatcher — repository retrieval and specialist-role routing for Claude Code and Codex
results.summary: Claude Code plugin and Codex skill pack that routes a task to one of 27 specialist roles (engineering, design, testing, research, writing, operations) and assembles a bounded context packet of source excerpts using symbols, source text, code relationships, Git history, and stack-trace frames — rather than a full-repo dump. Ships 79 bundled local skills, references 31 external skills, 8 workflow recipes, a registry of 19 MCP servers, and 50 detection signals for role/skill selection. Standard retrieval runs locally with no model or network calls; optional features (model-assisted reranking, an external 'Jev' decision-engine API, an Onboarding Explorer, procedural learning from recorded outcomes) are off by default and require the operator's own provider configuration. Installs via `claude plugin marketplace add` + `claude plugin install` for Claude Code, or `python3 install_codex.py` for Codex (installs one skill to `~/.agents/skills/agent-dispatcher/`). Invoked with `/agent-dispatcher:agent-dispatcher <request>` (Claude) or `$agent-dispatcher <request>` (Codex); roles can be forced directly (e.g. `$agent-dispatcher reviewer`). Verification is explicit: each role defines what evidence counts as done and reports which checks ran, passed, or were left unverified. Requires Python 3.10+, Git, and an authenticated Claude Code or Codex; native Windows is unsupported (WSL recommended). MIT license, single maintainer, repo created 2026-09-19 with ~50 GitHub stars and 4 forks as of this review.

results.name: open-webui
results.title: Open WebUI
results.summary: Leading self-hosted LLM web UI with RAG, pipelines, and enterprise auth — relevant infrastructure context but custom non-SPDX license limits adoption

results.name: lancedb
results.title: LanceDB
results.summary: Embedded serverless vector database built on Lance columnar format — runs in-process with no server, IVF/HNSW/PQ/RQ vector indexes + BM25 full-text, multimodal columns (text/image/video/audio), Git-style versioning, zero-copy reads, object storage backend (S3/GCS/AZ), DuckDB SQL integration, Python/TypeScript/Rust/REST SDKs; Apache-2.0

results.name: skill-search-mcp
results.title: Skill Search MCP

results.name: titans-atlas-cronus
results.title: Titans (Atlas + Cronus)
results.summary: Local-first, agent-first infrastructure pair from a solo AI-assisted builder — Atlas is persistent project memory (knowledge packages, typed graph, evidence/provenance, SQL, blobs, audit history; retrieval blends lexical + vector + graph + evidence, scoped per project/tenant), Cronus is durable execution (DAG workflows, scheduling, checkpoints, at-least-once retries with lease fencing, dead-letter, approval gates); shared MCP server over stdio plus REST/gRPC; free binaries, proprietary source, signed releases (SHA-256 + Ed25519); Windows/Linux

results.name: mempalace
results.title: MemPalace
results.summary: Local-first AI memory with 96.6% R@5 retrieval, 33 MCP tools, verbatim storage, and pluggable backends; strong benchmarks and Claude Code integration make it worth trialing

results.name: nashsu-llm-wiki
results.title: LLM Wiki (nashsu)
results.summary: Cross-platform Tauri desktop app implementing Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern — ingests documents (PDF/DOCX/PPTX/XLSX/EPUB/images/web clips) and incrementally compiles them into a persistent, interlinked wiki instead of re-deriving answers via RAG each query; ships a knowledge-graph visualizer (sigma.js/graphology, 4-signal relevance, Louvain community detection), optional LanceDB vector search, a tool-using chat agent, a local token-protected HTTP API plus MCP server for Claude Code/Codex, and an Obsidian-compatible vault output; ~21k GitHub stars; GPLv3

results.name: turboquant
results.title: TurboQuant — Extreme KV Cache Compression
results.summary: Foundational Google Research algorithm (ICLR 2026) for 3-4 bit KV cache compression with zero accuracy loss; growing downstream ecosystem but no single canonical package yet

results.name: opendataloader-pdf
results.title: OpenDataLoader PDF
results.summary: Top-benchmarked open-source PDF parser with bounding boxes, formula extraction, and RAG-ready output — worth piloting for bioinformatics literature ingestion before committing.

results.name: claude-mem
results.title: Claude Mem

results.name: karpathy-llm-wiki
results.title: Karpathy's LLM Wiki Pattern

results.name: production-agentic-platforms-2026
results.title: Production-Grade Agentic AI Platforms (2026 Evaluation)
results.summary: Practitioner evaluation of 5 agentic AI platforms for production use, ranked by orchestration, stateful workflows, human-in-the-loop, RAG, evals, observability, governance, and deployment flexibility: LangGraph (max engineering control), Microsoft Agent Framework (Azure enterprises), SimplAI (enterprise agent ops + governance), CrewAI (fast multi-agent dev), n8n (workflow automation + integrations); key lesson: 'can build an agent' ≠ 'can run agents in production' — observability, evaluation, governance, failure handling, deployment, and human-in-the-loop are the differentiators

results.name: kb
results.title: kb (Repo-Local Wiki + Agent Dispatch + Graph)

results.name: localai
results.title: LocalAI

results.name: book-to-skill
results.title: Book to Skill
results.summary: directly useful for computational biology methods PDFs

results.name: okf-agent-memory

results.name: amazon-s3-vectors
results.title: Amazon S3 Vectors

results.name: synapse-memory-layer

results.name: langchain
results.title: LangChain

results.name: paddleocr
results.title: PaddleOCR

results.name: mineru
results.title: MinerU
results.summary: Open-source document parsing engine by OpenDataLab — converts PDFs, images, Office docs (Word/PPT/Excel), EPUB, OFD, HTML/MHTML, CSV into LLM-ready Markdown/JSON with four quality tiers (flash/basic/standard/advanced); VLM+OCR dual engine supporting 109 languages; local-first with optional remote API; CLI with agent-oriented continuation/locator system; local document library with search/watch/scan; MCP server; integrations with LangChain, RAGFlow, Dify, FastGPT; Python >=3.10; Apache-2.0 with commercial threshold (100M MAU or $20M revenue); ~80k stars

results.name: tiktoken
results.title: tiktoken
results.summary: OpenAI's fast BPE tokenizer library — 3-6x faster than HuggingFace tokenizers; supports all OpenAI model encodings (o200k_base, cl100k_base, etc.); Python API for encode/decode, model-to-encoding lookup, custom encoding extension via plugin mechanism; educational submodule for visualizing BPE procedure; MIT

results.name: qwopus38-27b-flash
results.title: Qwopus3.8-27B-Flash
results.summary: Post-trained efficiency variant of Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid DeltaNet + attention architecture) focused on reducing unnecessary reasoning while preserving capability — +12.8% decoder throughput, MTP acceptance 66.1% to 80.7%, ~9.9% less total output with significantly fewer P95 runaway-reasoning cases; trades 1.45pp on MMLU-Pro (92.73% to 91.28%); 13/14 agent tasks passed at 99 tok/s on RTX 5090; trained with high-quality SFT (top 10% of 1.5M samples) + NVIDIA NeMo-RL GSPO; GGUF format

results.name: model-sovereignty-data-flywheel
results.title: Model Sovereignty and Data Flywheel Strategy
results.summary: Practitioner argument for organizations owning fine-tuned models rather than depending on closed API providers — cites GPT 5.6 Sol government-approval access restriction, declining GPU costs, competitive data flywheels as moat, and negative-example datasets for hallucination reduction

results.name: engram-learning-engine
results.title: Engram (Learning Engine)
results.summary: Evidence-based Claude Code learning plugin — FSRS spaced repetition, free-recall verification with blind assessor grading, first-principles concept graphs, interactive HTML explorables; three commands (/learn, /review, /coach); Python 3 stdlib only, local JSON storage

results.name: n8n-mcp
results.title: n8n MCP Server
results.summary: powerful workflow automation bridge but heavy dependency; evaluate when pipeline orchestration needs outgrow kb dispatch

results.name: deepseek-v4-flash-kv-cache-architecture
results.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash KV Cache Architecture
results.summary: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash transformer architecture redesign targeting KV cache reduction — Cross-layer Encoder-Decoder (CED) splits 20 encoder + 20 decoder layers so prompt tokens skip decoder entirely; cross-layer attention sharing (Full/Reindex/Reuse modes) shares KV across layers; global cache compressed to FP4 with 128-token bounded replay for local states; 4x smaller global cache, 8x smaller persistent cache vs V4 Flash

results.name: conductor-oss
results.title: Conductor OSS
results.summary: Open-source durable execution platform (ex-Netflix) for microservices, AI agents, and adaptive workflow graphs — JSON-defined orchestration with durable state, native LLM tasks, MCP tool calling, human approval, dynamic fork/join, DO_WHILE loops, polyglot workers (Java/Python/Go/JS/C#/Ruby/Rust), 5 persistence backends, 6 message brokers; Claude Code plugin; Apache-2.0

results.name: socratic
results.title: Socratic
results.summary: Self-interrogation skill packaging 697 engineering questions across 15 domains — agent silently works through relevant questions, reads codebase, applies defaults, and only escalates genuine authority decisions to user; Core (90 questions) and Full (697) modes; knowledge-backed packs for specialist depth; MIT

results.name: qdrant
results.title: Qdrant
results.summary: Rust-based vector similarity search engine and database — HNSW with inline payload filtering, dense/sparse/multi-vector search, hybrid search with RRF/DBSF fusion, TurboQuant 4-bit/8-bit compression, GPU-accelerated indexing, distributed sharding and replication, gRPC and REST APIs, Edge variant for in-process use; Apache-2.0

results.name: milvus
results.title: Milvus

results.name: cobalt
results.title: Cobalt

results.name: agentic-memory-benchmark

results.summary: Benchmark of 8 AI agent memory systems across 2176 tasks (272 scored per system: 200 fact-recall + 72 never-stored hallucination checks), in which a plain curated markdown wiki outscored all commercial memory products tested

results.name: nvk-llm-wiki
results.title: llm-wiki (nvk)
results.summary: Claude Code plugin (with ports for Codex, DeepSeek Harness, OpenCode, and generic SKILL.md agents) implementing Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern — treats raw sources as immutable "source code" and the LLM as a "compiler" that synthesizes them into a structured, source-linked wiki; organizes topics as isolated sub-wikis in a hub, runs parallel multi-agent research (5/8/10 agents per depth mode), and enforces that no wiki page exists without a cited source; commands include /wiki init, /wiki:research, /wiki:thesis, /wiki:query, /wiki:ingest, /wiki:compile; ~1.5k GitHub stars; MIT

results.name: anthropic-global-workspace
results.title: A Global Workspace in Language Models
results.summary: Anthropic interpretability research identifying the "J-space" — a small set of internal neural patterns in Claude that function as a global workspace for deliberate reasoning, reportable thoughts, and internal monitoring; includes J-lens technique for reading model thoughts not expressed in output

results.name: claude-skills-rezvani
results.title: Claude Skills (Rezvani)
results.summary: 355-skill library for 13 AI coding tools — 18 domains (engineering, marketing, product, compliance, C-level advisory, research, finance, business ops), 602 stdlib-only Python CLI tools, 711 reference templates; cross-platform (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Aider, Windsurf, and 7 more); MIT

results.name: frontier
results.title: Frontier
results.summary: Well-architected multi-harness orchestration runtime for Claude Code; early preview but the token-economics argument and delegation model are sound

results.name: agent-software-engineering-fundamentals
results.title: Software Engineering Fundamentals for AI Agents (schema-first memory, deterministic guardrails)
results.summary: Practitioner discussion arguing most agent memory, prompt-injection, and goal-hijacking problems are solved by pre-LLM software-engineering basics — design the memory data model first (what is stored, how it changes behavior, TTL and scope) instead of free-text dumps; treat LLM output as untrusted input validated against schemas; model the agent as a workflow (defined state + allowed transitions, model proposes moves that code checks); least-privilege scoped credentials, tool allowlists, process/data isolation, audit logs; reserve human approval for irreversible or boundary-crossing actions and show the exact payload to avoid approval fatigue

results.name: state-of-context-engineering-2026
results.title: The State of Context Engineering 2026 (Redis)
results.summary: Redis-published survey report on context-engineering maturity among IT/AI infrastructure leaders: defines context engineering as deciding what an agent sees at each step (navigable, fresh, fast, compounding); reports 79% call context 'very important' yet 81% sit at the two earliest maturity stages (ad hoc/exploratory) and only 4% report reaching the 'compounding' stage; cites Gartner ('context engineering is in, prompt engineering is out', July 2025) and Cognizant's plan to train/deploy 1,000 context engineers (Aug 2025); promotes Redis's own Iris product and a gated 'Context Engineering Maturity Model' self-assessment/full report.

results.name: suede-creator-skills

results.name: pi-system-one
results.title: pi-system-one

results.name: benzi
results.title: Benzi
results.summary: Code-intelligence agent/tool that compiles a codebase into a queryable index (tree-sitter-based: symbols, call edges, references, class inheritance) before answering questions or editing, instead of grepping/globbing raw source into an LLM's context window. Ships as a VS Code extension, a headless CLI (benzi-headless), and an MCP server (benzi-mcp) for other agents, sharing one login. The VS Code/CLI agent additionally runs a runtime tracer, gates edits against a fresh parse, checks blast radius before/after writes, self-escalates to a larger model mid-task, and keeps persistent per-repo memory with one-step rollback. Covers 10 languages (Python deepest) plus an HTML/CSS/DOM-JS markup engine; 35+ query tools. Free during beta, BYOK against Anthropic/OpenAI/DeepSeek/Groq/Kimi/compatible APIs; self-published 82.4% SWE-bench Verified result. The GitHub repo is documentation only (no source), with GitHub reporting no recognized open-source license (license key: other/NOASSERTION).

results.name: harnessx
results.title: HarnessX
results.summary: Python agent-harness foundry from the Darwin Agent Team separating model (ModelConfig) from behavior (HarnessConfig): a 9-dimension processor pipeline (context, control, evaluation, memory, multi-model, observability, tools, plus providers/plugins) composed with a `|` operator, plus two self-reported evolution loops — a meta-harness that auto-searches processor/config combinations, and RL fine-tuning (via VERL) on reward-annotated run trajectories. MIT-licensed, v0.1.0/Beta. Companion papers: HarnessX (arXiv:2606.14249) and a follow-on, DarwinX (arXiv:2608.07545).

results.name: headroom
results.title: Headroom

results.name: qwen38-27b-200k-on-16gb
results.title: Qwen 3.8 27B at 200K Context on 16GB VRAM (tutorial)
results.summary: Practitioner recipe for running Qwen 3.8 27B UD-IQ4_XS at ~196K context and 50 t/s on a single RTX 5070 Ti (16GB) — prune non-ASCII rows from the embedding table and LM head (~700MB, ASCII-condensed variant published), offload the embedding table to CPU, disable MTP, use adaptive-KV streaming (llama.cpp fork) to page KV cache from host RAM, and quantize cache Q8 K / Q4 V

results.name: cline
results.title: Cline
results.summary: Open-source autonomous coding agent distributed as a VS Code extension, JetBrains plugin (early access), SDK, and CLI — file editing, terminal command execution, browser automation, and MCP tool integration with human-in-the-loop approval by default (diff review, checkpoints to undo agent work, optional auto-approve); project rules via .clinerules files; MCP Marketplace and hosted SaaS (Cline.bot) with free/paid/enterprise tiers; developed by Cline Bot Inc.; TypeScript; ~71k GitHub stars, 5M+ VS Code installs; Apache-2.0

results.name: seven-levels-of-observability
results.title: The 7 Levels of Observability
results.summary: A content creator's seven-stage observability maturity ladder — logs, metrics, traces, correlation (shared request ID across logs/traces), alerts, SLOs (SLI/SLO/SLA), and cardinality management — presented as a progression where each stage answers a question the previous one couldn't (what happened, is it trending, where is the time going, why, before users notice, is the target at risk, can we afford to measure it). Not a single named industry-standard framework: published observability maturity models elsewhere range from 3 pillars (logs/metrics/traces) to 4-5 level maturity scales (e.g. Last9, codefarm.in) covering the same underlying concepts — structured logs with trace IDs, OpenTelemetry-style distributed tracing, SLO/error-budget-driven alerting, and cardinality limits on metric labels — under different level counts and names.

results.name: vector-database-basics-hnsw
results.title: Vector Database Basics: HNSW (Tiger Data / Timescale)
results.summary: Tiger Data (Timescale) blog explainer on HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) vector indexing: describes HNSW's skip-list-inspired multi-layer graph (sparse long-edge upper layers for coarse navigation, dense lower layers for fine-grained search), and its use with pgvector/Timescale Vector on Postgres via the m (max connections per layer) and ef_construction (build-time candidate list size) parameters that trade index size/build time for search accuracy.
